editorNote: Gold's September slide and a security breach at a major exchange frame the day, while bitcoin heads for a monthly gain. Two of the three items are market data; the third is a disclosure from Bitget that its own account of the attack is still being filled in.

stories.headline: Gold rebounds 1.4% to about $4,185 after Monday's 3.1% drop, but yields and the dollar cap the bounce
stories.summary: Gold rose 1.39% to US$4,184.97 an ounce on Tuesday after falling 3.12% on Monday; weak job-openings and consumer-confidence data cut the odds of an October Fed hike from 70.9% to about 51.5%. The 10-year yield held at 5.25% and the dollar index reached a two-month high of 101.37.
stories.whyItMatters: Gold regained only a fraction of Monday's losses, with high yields and a stronger dollar still weighing on it.

sourceLinks.title: Gold, silver, precious metals — Wednesday, September 30, 2026 (Rio Times)

stories.headline: Bitget resumes withdrawals in phases after a $387.5 million hack it blames on North Korean actors
stories.summary: Bitget says $387.5 million was moved to attacker-controlled addresses across several blockchains on September 25, via a zero-day flaw in third-party security products, and its CEO attributes the attack to North Korean hackers. Bitcoin withdrawals are back, USDT is due September 30, and other tokens and fiat by October 2; a 5% recovery bounty is on offer.
stories.whyItMatters: The exchange says user balances are unaffected and its Protection Fund covers the loss, but the attribution and root cause are Bitget's and its investigators' claims.

sourceLinks.title: Bitget resumes Bitcoin withdrawals after $387.5 million crypto heist (BleepingComputer)

stories.headline: Bitcoin sits near $83,800 as it heads for a September gain of about 7%, ending a 'Red September' pattern
stories.summary: Bitcoin traded at $83,767 and ether at $2,686.56 on the morning of September 30, up 6.9% and 8.9% for the month. Bitcoin has now finished September higher four years running, though it is still down 26.9% from a year ago.
stories.whyItMatters: September has closed in the red in eight of the last 13 years, and bitcoin remains well below its 2025 all-time high.
